chapter_seo_title: Dao Gui Yi Xian Ch. 437: The Truth of Great Qi & Intercalation
chapter_meta_description: Li Huowang learns the truth: Zhuge Yuan’s Great Qi is a parallel history, not the past. He uses the Intercalating the Five Phases ritual from the Thousand Greats Record to save Zhuge Yuan from a Siming’s eye.

twitter_description: Li Huowang discovers Zhuge Yuan’s Great Qi is a parallel timeline. The ultimate price of the *Thousand Greats Record* is paid.

lore_anchors.definition: An ancient Chinese kingdom (1046–221 BCE); in the novel, the “Great Qi” is a parallel history accessed through a Heart-Core, not a literal past.
An Arbiter of Fate; a high-dimensional deity in the Dao-Twisted World whose presence can rewrite reality and cause ontological breakdown.

A forbidden ritual from the *Thousand Greats Record* where the practitioner sacrifices their five visceral organs to merge their senses and host the primordial god Bashe, granting temporary immunity to cognitive interference.
A primordial god of pain worshipped by the Ao-Jing Sect; it can only be perceived by merging the five senses into a single awareness.
A twisted expansion of the Buddhist Eight Sufferings; implies a cultivation path that weaponizes a granular spectrum of emotional pain.
A major Buddhist temple in Great Qi; in this timeline, its abbot is the Mad Monk, making it a powerful, protective institution rather than a corrupt one.
The five yin organs in Traditional Chinese Medicine: Heart, Liver, Spleen, Lung, and Kidneys—each corresponds to one of the Five Phases.

cultural_notes_faq.a: A rare human constitution that acts as a door to an alternate timeline or "history." Zhuge Yuan's Heart-Core lets him access the world of Great Qi.

cultural_notes_faq.q: What does "Intercalating the Five Phases" do?
cultural_notes_faq.a: It sacrifices the user's five visceral organs to allow the primordial god Bashe to fill the void with parasitic worms, granting immunity to all other spiritual or cognitive interference, but the user's body is consumed.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Is Great Qi the past or a different timeline?
cultural_notes_faq.a: It is confirmed to be a parallel history (timeline), not a literal past. Li Huowang's realization reframes all previous encounters as visits to a different branch of reality.
